pr_title: Deprecate k_mem_pool API, remove sys_mem_pool allocator
pr_body:
The k_heap/sys_heap code has been default for a release, so it's time to deprecate the old allocator.

This eliminates the older CONFIG_MEM_POOL_HEAP_BACKEND kconfig, effectively making it true always and removing the ability for applications to request the older pool engine.  It then deprecates the older APIs, leaving them in place for internal users as a "Z" API.

There are still a few users of the older API internally that will need cleanup (**edit: not anymore, it's 100% gone in the current version**).  I'll submit those separately I think, I'm not sure if those are in scope for 2.4 or not:

* k_malloc and the system pool are still implemented in terms of mem_pool, even though those are just wrappers now.  It should be directly on top of a k_heap.

* The per-thread resource pools likewise are mem_pools still.  This should be k_heap's instead.

* Mailbox has a API that will retrieve a message into a newly-allocated heap block.  This API is weird and itself deprecated, but if we decide we actually want to preserve the functionality it will need some kind of new variant.

* Similarly pipe has block usage internally.

And there are two places where the underlying sys_heap allocator still gets used:

* The minimal libc malloc() implementation is on top of sys_heap instead of k_malloc.  I'm not sure why, but this needs some kind of port.

* The lib/gui/lvgl code has an internal sys_mem_pool and needs a port to sys_heap (not hard to write, but I have no idea how to test it)

Fixes #24358
pr_comments: Ugh, it collides.  Sorry, I did this on a week-stale master.  Will get that cleaned up.

I'm not clear on how #24358 is a bug, let alone having a release-blocking priority, except as a means of getting this late change into 2.4.0.  And I've been told before that stage of release cycle is not a valid reason for rejecting a PR.

But from policy discussion heard at the last TSC regarding criteria for accepting late addition of new boards I need to ask: If a PR like this came three days before release from anybody other than a platinum member company, would people be seriously considering merging it into the release when it passes?

> I'm not clear on how #24358 is a bug

It's a bug because we have two mechanisms in the kernel which do the same thing, and we do not want to maintain both, particularly not in the second LTS release.

> If a PR like this came three days before release from anybody other than a platinum member company, would people be seriously considering merging it into the release when it passes?

seriously? What exactly is the purpose of creating releases and having almost 4 weeks of bug fix and stabilization period if we do not address issues like this? 

This was a bug when it was created in April, move to an Enhancement because it did not happen for 2.3 with clear documentation in the issue itself that it should go into 2.4. This had nothing to do with membership level and it is disappointing to hear that TBH. This is not something someone is pushing for to get a feature in late in the game, this actually removes duplication and confusion. So there is no direct and "personal" gain from doing this.

Seriously, the need to do this has been known for months.  Why is it being done so late, and why is it being forced/enabled by giving #24358 a release-blocking priority?  Zephyr's ability to plan what goes into a release, and track its progress, is disappointingly weak.

I do feel that part of the criteria for accepting PRs in the stabilization period should be the risk of destabilizing, invalidating all the testing that's been done, and introducing build warnings in out of tree applications and downstream forks that have been faithfully tracking the release and suddenly have to make changes to accommodate a last minute API deprecation.

That there are so many remaining in-tree uses that fail CI because of the new deprecation suggests this isn't a baseless concern.

And I remain very skeptical that this would be getting this level of attention and support if a random community contributor had proposed it at this point.

This also needs to deprecate `k_pipe_block_put()`

AFAICT the full set of APIs to deprecate is:
  * `k_mbox_data_block_get()`
  * `k_pipe_block_put()`
  * `K_MEM_POOL_DEFINE()`
  * `k_mem_pool_alloc()`
  * `k_mem_pool_free()`
  * `k_mem_pool_free_id()`
  * `SYS_MEM_POOL_DEFINE()`
  * `sys_mem_pool_init()`
  * `sys_mem_pool_alloc()`
  * `sys_mem_pool_free()`
  * `sys_mem_pool_try_expand_inplace()`

Since this is now in scope for early 2.5 and not 2.4, I would prefer if these deprecation PRs converted internal kernel usage to k_heap / sys_heap rather than introducing these z_ variants.

> And I remain very skeptical that this would be getting this level of attention and support if a random community contributor had proposed it at this point.

you have examples of this ever happening? Can you document that non-random users did get a pass just because they are platinum or whatever? This accusation you are making here is very serious.

We do have a process to deal with this. If it was not raised as a blocker then we would have never been able to to make a decision about this and come up with the compromise we reached. Just because you think it is a bad move does not mean we are not able to address the issue and  come to a conclusion.
@andyross @andrewboie could we pick this up now that 2.4 has been released? let's not wait until the next release is close yet again.

> @andyross @andrewboie could we pick this up now that 2.4 has been released? let's not wait until the next release is close yet again.

Let's get this moving again

> Let's get this moving again

@andyross  already working on this.

Resurrect this guy with a more invasive change.  Contains the old deprecation, and also a complete removal of the older sys_mem_pool allocator backend.  That code (and a bunch of tests specific to it) is now gone, the only allocator we ship is the new one.

The compatibility API (which implements the old scheme in terms of the new allocator) remains in place as "z_mem_pool" for the benefit of a few in-tree spots that still use it and are difficult for me to test directly (mostly driver code for devices I don't have).  We can address these piecewise as we find maintainers able to validate, that stuff is all boilerplate.

And this does not contain a patch that actually removes the deprecated APIs.  I'm still not clear on the project management intent there as to whether that should happen this release or next.

did you miss one?

```

/workdir/zephyr/tests/kernel/mem_protect/syscalls/src/main.c:392:2: error: 'z_thread_resource_pool_assign' is deprecated [-Werror=deprecated-declarations]
--



```

> did you miss one?

Yeah, last minute goof.  That function is an internal wrapper, it's not supposed to be deprecated.  This happened because there had been a "temporarily undeprecated" k_* function there at one point (i.e. to suppress the deprecation warnings while I worked on somethign else), which worked by commenting the function out with a C++ comment I knew would get caught later (e.g. "//__deprecated // FIXME reenable"), which did indeed get caught in a final checkpatch.  But then I blindly reenabled it forgetting that this was now an internal function that didn't need to be deprecated and pushed before re-running the whole sanitycheck.

Probably too much detail.  Easy fix.  Will push as soon as my rebased tree completes its check.

I'd been assuming those weird BSIM errors (in code that has nothing to do with mem_pool) were an upstream thing, but they turned out to be a latent bug with a header (missing stdint.h) that the removal of mempool_sys.h exposed.  Fixed.

Resurrect this guy with a rebase, and a few extra patches that port the tree internals away from the old API, remove the old API entirely, and then remove the wrappers.  Should be good to go per existing comments.  We'll see what CI says.
Heh, usb_dc_nrfx was one of the blind changes, isn't part of a default sanitycheck, but is part of CI.  Fixed typo, repushed.
nrf52_bsim is unrelated and caused by #29810

issue_context.title: deprecate and remove old k_mem_pool / sys_mem_pool APIs
issue_context.body:
We have replaced the mem pool APIs with the new k_heap/sys_heap APIs. We don't need to keep maintaining two APIs for doing the same thing, and should aim to remove the k_mem_pool and sys_mem_pool APIs from the kernel.

The first step is to `__deprecate` them all, and change any use within Zephyr to use k_heap/sys_heap instead.

The `k_pipe_block_put()` API will need to be adjusted as it takes a `k_mem_block` as an argument. I couldn't find any other public APIs which would need to be changed.
comments: @andyross and @andrewboie we need this for 2.3.0. Any timeline for a PR?

I was honestly expecting this to wait for a release before deprecation, to reduce churn.  The original idea, I thought, was that in 2.3 apps would have the new backend by default but no requirement to move away from the old APIs, then later we'd start moving things away.

Some of this, like the direct mem_pool APIs, is straightforward.  Also we could rework k_malloc/k_free in terms of the immediate API and not a double-wrapper.  The thread memory pools are coded to the old API but could easily be moved to the new one.

But the old pool scheme has its fingers in other places too, like the k_mem_block abstraction used as a handle, which would be an API change if we want to "fix" that (though for a first cut we could just add a constructor for one from a k_heap+pointer tuple)   Also both mailbox and pipe will allocate on the behalf of their users, so they need porting.  There are probably others I forget.

The early stuff in that list is easy and can be done this week.  The later bits may take some thought and argument.
I don't think this should be a high priority bug for 2.3 I think this can wait until 2.4. @carlescufi can you share some details on your reasoning for making this a blocker?

> reasoning for making this a blocker?
reasoning is the fact that if we need to deprecate, then it has to happen in 2.3, otherwise might end up with old APIs. 


>  have the new backend by default but no requirement to move away from the old APIs, then later we'd start moving things away.

Ok, if we deprecate this in 2.4, then we should be able to drop legacy in 2.6 (LTS), i think this works fine.

@carlescufi  lets move this to 2.4..

This should be a bug and be fixed for 2.4. It was already something that had to be fixed for 2.3 and never happened.

@nashif @MaureenHelm do you agree?

OK, sounds good.   I'll provide the deprecation patch as soon as I get another spin of the SOF PR up, that one is easy.  Note it will end up needing to remove a few tests though.  Post-deprecation, there needs to be a new API to convert a heap block to an old-style "mem block" for the oddball APIs that use those.
Consensus in #28611 is that this should be pushed to 2.5

> Consensus in #28611 is that this should be pushed to 2.5

Nevertheless, thank you @andyross for putting together this PR so quickly.
